name_reason: Name already matches the convention data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> and reflects both the data type (_ptr = pointer slot) and the purpose (field-map per-tile-event consumed flags). The '_ptr' suffix is correct: the global is a 4-byte uint32 BSS slot holding a malloc(0x20) heap address (write at main 0x25d3d: PUSH 0x20; CALL malloc; MOV [0x53ad5],EAX). No Ghidra address residue in the name; 'field_map' is the domain. No change needed.
purpose: Base pointer to a 32-byte heap block of per-tile-event 'consumed' booleans (one byte per field-map terrain_class) so each field-map tile event (chest/gold/scripted) fires only once.
logic_summary: uint32 BSS pointer slot. Sole writer = main @ 0x25BF4: data_fd2_field_map_tile_event_consumed_flags_ptr = (uint32)malloc(0x20), allocating the 32-byte block once at startup. fd2_load_save_and_init_engine @ 0x10010 memmove's 0x20 bytes from the save buffer (pBuf+0x30A3) into it to restore per-event state on load. Readers (fd2_handle_tile_event_interaction @ 0x190AC, fd2_tick_tile_event_animations @ 0x122A8, ~60 chapter event handlers, field menu / battle init dispatchers) index the block as flags[terrain_class]: gate with flags[class]!=0 -> skip (already fired) and set flags[class]=1 after a tile-event item/gold pickup. The 5-bit terrain_class index range 0..31 is exactly why the block is 32 bytes (malloc(0x20)).
datatype: uint32 (4-byte BSS pointer slot; points to a malloc'd unsigned char[0x20] one-byte-per-terrain_class flag array)
element_semantics: The pointer itself is one 32-bit heap address. The pointed-to block: 32 entries of 1 byte, indexed by the tile's 5-bit terrain_class (0..31); each byte is a boolean (1 = that terrain_class's tile event has already been consumed/fired, 0 = not yet).
comment_original_issue: Existing block was accurate and thorough; only minor imprecision: it called the index a '16-bit tile id'. The true index is the tile's 5-bit terrain_class (0..31), which is the load-bearing fact explaining the malloc(0x20) size (one slot per terrain_class).
notes: Single WRITE xref (main @ 0x25d3d) confirms pointer-set-once semantics; ~60 READ xrefs all use it as base of a byte array. Neighbor globals at 0x53ad1 (data_fd2_resource_portrait_sheet_ptr) and 0x53ad9 (data_fd2_dialog_last_action_sprite_id_param) are distinct, confirming 0x53ad5 is a standalone 4-byte slot. is_const=false: there is a write-xref from the game (main writes the pointer; load_save memmoves into the pointed-to block). Ghidra had no data plate at 0x53ad5; created a concise one (690 chars) from the src conclusion. src comment block (main.c lines 562-582) lightly augmented to replace '16-bit tile id' with '5-bit terrain_class (0..31)'.
